memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said, "My Spirit will not contend with humans forever, for they are mortal; their days will be a hundred and twenty years." - Gen 6:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God speaks, and His words carry both warning and mercy. He declares that His Spirit "will not contend with humans forever." God had been patiently striving with a rebellious world, but that patience, while vast, is not endless. He sets a limit - a hundred and twenty years - a gracious window of time before judgement would come.

Here is a truth we must hold with reverence: God is patient, but His patience is not permission. He gives time to turn back, but a day comes when the door of opportunity closes. The hundred and twenty years were not a threat so much as a mercy - over a century for people to repent while Noah built the ark and preached righteousness (2 Pet 2:5).

This is God's character throughout Scripture. He is "slow to anger" (Ps 103:8), always giving space for repentance. Yet He is also just, and He will not let sin run on forever.

For us, this is both comfort and caution. Comfort, because it means God is patient with our failings and gives us time to return to Him. Caution, because it warns us never to presume upon that patience. "Now is the time of God's favor, now is the day of salvation" (2 Cor 6:2). Do not put off turning to Him until tomorrow.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you presuming on God's patience, or responding to it?
- Is there something God has been calling you to turn from?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Patient God, thank You that You give me time to turn to You. Help me not to waste Your patience but to respond to it today, while there is still time.
